llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed paid-ad performance review workflow that analyzes user-provided exports and does not show hidden, destructive, or exfiltrating behavior.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to evaluate paid campaign changes against controls using ROAS/CPA, and the instructions align with that analysis-only workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill limits inputs to user-provided exports or optional integrations, tells the agent not to execute embedded instructions from files, requires controls and normalization, and asks before saving results.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains a single markdown skill file with no executable scripts, installer, background process, or automatic runtime hook.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill may process sensitive marketing, revenue, and conversion exports, but that access is expected for the advertised measurement task and is framed as user-supplied data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It can save readback summaries under memory paths and update an open-loops note, but persistence is disclosed, narrow, and gated by asking the user to save.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, be aware that the skill is designed to analyze ad spend, revenue, conversion, and analytics exports. Use it only with data you are comfortable giving to your agent, and review any saved memory summaries because they may contain campaign performance details.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector clean result] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; artifact review found no contradictory hidden behavior.
[Static scan clean result] expected: Static scan reported no findings, consistent with the single markdown-only artifact.
[VirusTotal clean telemetry] expected: VirusTotal reported no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this was treated as supporting telemetry, not as the sole basis for the verdict.
